arxiv-2107-04595.title: Energy balance for nonholonomic nonlinear systems
arxiv-2107-04595.creator: F. Talamucci
arxiv-2107-04595.description: Abstract 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification: 37J60, 70F25, 70H03. Keywords: Lagrange’s equations of motion - Nonholonomic systems - Nonlinear kinematic constraints - Equations of Voronec type - Generalized Theorem of energy. Abstract . We consider nonholonomic systems with nonlinear restrictions with respect to the velocities. The mathematical problem is formulated by means of the Voronec equations extended to the nonlinear case.

arxiv-2202-13661.title: Edge-Cut Width: An Algorithmically Driven Analogue of Treewidth Based on Edge Cuts
arxiv-2202-13661.creator: Cornelius Brand, Esra Ceylan, Robert Ganian, Christian Hatschka, Viktoriia Korchemna
arxiv-2202-13661.description: Abstract Decompositional parameters such as treewidth are commonly used to obtain fixed-parameter algorithms for NP -hard graph problems. For problems that are W ​ [ 1 ] {\mbox{{{W}}}}[1] -hard parameterized by treewidth, a natural alternative would be to use a suitable analogue of treewidth that is based on edge cuts instead of vertex separators.

arxiv-2302-08170.title: Evidence for non-thermal X-ray emission from the double WR colliding-wind binary Apep
arxiv-2302-08170.creator: S. del Palacio, F. García, M. De Becker, D. Altamirano, V. Bosch-Ramon, P. Benaglia, B. Marcote, G. E. Romero
arxiv-2302-08170.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by S. del Palacio, F. García, M. De Becker, D. Altamirano, V. Bosch-Ramon, P. Benaglia, B. Marcote, G. E. Romero. Massive colliding-wind binaries (CWBs) can be non-thermal sources. The emission produced in their wind-collision region (WCR) encodes information of both the shocks properties and the relativistic electrons accelerated in them.

arxiv-2307-03071.creator: MARCO CALAUTTI 1, SERGIO GRECO 2, CRISTIAN MOLINARO 2 and IRINA TRUBITSYNA 2 1 DI, University of Milan, Italy 2 DIMES, University of Calabria, Italy
arxiv-2307-03071.description: Abstract Data exchange, the problem of transferring data from a source schema to a target schema, has been studied for several years. The semantics of answering positive queries over the target schema has been defined in early work, but little attention has been paid to more general queries.

arxiv-2311-07629.title: Note on the second eigenvalue of regular graphs
arxiv-2311-07629.creator: Igor Balla, Eero Räty, Benny Sudakov, István Tomon
arxiv-2311-07629.description: Abstract The goal of this expository note is to give a short, self-contained proof of nearly optimal lower bounds for the second largest eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix of regular graphs. This is a companion note to [ 4 ] .

arxiv-2403-02471.title: Anisotropic examples of inflation-generating initial conditions for the big bang
arxiv-2403-02471.creator: Eric Ling, Annachiara Piubello
arxiv-2403-02471.description: Abstract The inflationary scenario, which states that the early universe underwent a brief but dramatic period of accelerated spatial expansion, has become the current paradigm of early universe cosmology. Although inflationary cosmology has its many successes, it does not (as of yet) have the status of an established physical theory.

arxiv-2410-23412.title: BAMITA: Bayesian Multiple Imputation for Tensor Arrays
arxiv-2410-23412.creator: Ziren Jiang, Gen Li, Eric F. Lock
arxiv-2410-23412.description: Abstract Data increasingly take the form of a multi-way array, or tensor, in several biomedical domains. Such tensors are often incompletely observed. For example, we are motivated by longitudinal microbiome studies in which several timepoints are missing for several subjects. There is a growing literature on missing data imputation for tensors.

pmc-11527426.title: Schistosoma antigens: A future clinical magic bullet for autoimmune diseases?
pmc-11527426.creator: Mphatso Mayuni Chaponda, Ho Yin Pekkle Lam
pmc-11527426.description: Autoimmune diseases are characterized by dysregulated immunity against self-antigens. Current treatment of autoimmune diseases largely relies on suppressing host immunity to prevent excessive inflammation. Other immunotherapy options, such as cytokine or cell-targeted therapies, have also been used. However, most patients do not benefit from these therapies as recurrence of the disease usually occurs.

pmc-11583107.title: Thyroglossal Duct Cysts (TGDC) in the Elderly Population: The Role of Conservative Management
pmc-11583107.creator: Maria K Pomponio, Keith R Conti, Jason F Ohlstein, Irfan Khan, Thomas Koch
pmc-11583107.description: Sistrunk procedure is the treatment for thyroglossal duct cysts (TGDC), the majority of which occur in children. TGDC are very rare in the elderly and account for under 2% of cases. Management in this population, where risks of surgery may outweigh benefits, is unclear. Here we present two cases of elderly patients with asymptomatic to mildly symptomatic TGDC.

pmc-13134657.title: Discrepancies Between Point of Care and Central Laboratory Sodium and Potassium Measurements in ICU: Analytical Biases and Physician Awareness
pmc-13134657.creator: Nadia Nakhil, Samer Najem, Rania Driss, Tarek Chaabouni, Nicolas Dufour
pmc-13134657.description: OBJECTIVES:Blood electrolyte panels, especially sodium ion (Na+) and potassium ion (K+), are fundamental and routine tests. In critical care settings, these measurements are typically performed by central laboratories using indirect potentiometry (IP) or via point-of-care blood gas analyzers using direct potentiometry (DP).

pmc-13208800.title: Association of Plasma IL-6 with Indoor Radon Exposure in Children with Non-Allergic Asthma
pmc-13208800.creator: Saleh Alsulami, Youn Soo Jung, Kari Nadeau, Perdita Permaul, Longxiang Li, Petros Koutrakis, Jonathan M. Gaffin, Wanda Phipatanakul, Tina M. Banzon
pmc-13208800.description: Background/Objectives: Radon exposure has recently been associated with asthma morbidity, including increased airway inflammation and school absenteeism in children, though limited data on underlying biological mechanisms exist. Interleukin-6 (IL-6), a pleiotropic cytokine implicated in both Type 2-low airway inflammation and radon-related lung carcinogenesis, may represent a key mechanistic link between radon exposure and asthma morbidity.
